subject.title: WhatsApp: Gemini thinking tags (<think>/<final>) still leak after #6328 fix

question: For strict sanitizer mode, should an unclosed `<think>` payload that contains a `<final>` opener recover only the final-answer body, or should OpenClaw keep the current fully wrapped unclosed-tag recovery behavior even when it may expose reasoning before the final boundary?
rationale: The code can be changed narrowly, but the choice sets a security boundary between hiding private reasoning and preserving answers from malformed model output, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics alone.

options.title: Recover only final-answer text
options.body: Treat `<final>` as the visible boundary before unclosed-thinking recovery, hide preceding reasoning, and add WhatsApp/Telegram/shared sanitizer regression coverage.

options.title: Keep current recovery semantics
options.body: Accept the risk that fully wrapped malformed reasoning may be delivered when it avoids dropping the whole answer, relying on native Gemini mode to reduce the trigger.

options.title: Defer to broader channel policy
options.body: Leave this issue blocked behind the larger internal-text delivery policy work, acknowledging that this specific malformed-tag path remains shipped meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Recover only final-answer text
recommendation.body: Treat `<final>` as the visible boundary before unclosed-thinking recovery, hide preceding reasoning, and add WhatsApp/Telegram/shared sanitizer regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is centered on shared sanitizer semantics and final-tag/reasoning recovery behavior where steipete has the clearest recent history.
